event.hall_dance.10.text: Into the hall box, every coin. Except one. Marcus, that one's yours. Spend it on something that isn't wood.
event.hall_dance.10.why: hands Marcus the coin so his 'One coin. One dance.' answers her directly

event.tilda_heart6.intro.text: Turn the sign to Closed, would you? Just for an hour. I do the books when it's quiet. Your chair's free.
event.tilda_heart6.intro.why: calls back the chair from heart 5

dlg.tilda.hours.1.text: I tell myself Wetherell isn't shrinking. Then the bell goes four times before lunch. What do you think?
dlg.tilda.hours.1.why: drops 'twice', which heart 5 already uses for the bell

dlg.tilda.hours.r1.text: Together. Now that's a plan I'd stock. Bring ideas. I'll bring the tea, and the good cups.
dlg.tilda.hours.r1.why: heart 5 already ends on Thursday; no second day promise

event.tilda_heart8.intro.text: Yearly stocktake, and I need strong arms. Shift the flour? There's a tin back there I've been carefully not looking at.
event.tilda_heart8.intro.why: separates it from Stocktake Saturday; echoes heart 2's 'I haven't looked'

event.tilda_heart10.give.text: Pumpkin pie, still warm. Take it. And yes, that's your farm on my sign. Supplier. In paint, not chalk.
event.tilda_heart10.give.why: no longer claims the card's first pie, which the keep and bake branches contradict

event.tilda_heart10.thanks.text: {if choice:card.share}I copied the recipe for every kitchen, and put your name at the bottom. In chalk, so it can grow.{else}{if choice:card.bake}That Saturday you stood by the oven so I couldn't back out. This is the second one. Easier.{else}The card's still in its tin, where it's happiest. This one's from memory. Close enough to count.{/if}{/if}
event.tilda_heart10.thanks.why: each branch now remembers heart 8's choice exactly

dlg.tilda.birthday.r0.text: Oh. Well. That goes at the top of the slate, where I'll see it first thing every morning.
dlg.tilda.birthday.r0.why: 'capitals' was wallpaper; it belongs to the Felix thin-ice joke

event.tilda_birthday.after.text: {if choice:bday.tilda.wish}Top of the slate. It reads very well from the street.{else}{if choice:bday.tilda.flower}The flower's in the window. Half the village asked who sent it. I said an account in good standing.{else}An hour off! I read a whole chapter upstairs. The shop survived. I'm slightly offended.{/if}{/if}

dlg.story.notes.tilda.1.text: ...Well. Now you know who's been doing it. Wren mustn't find out. She'd want a cut.
dlg.story.notes.tilda.1.why: heart 6 already closes on 'not a word to Felix'

dlg.story.pumpkin.felix.1.text: Felix. Is that my prize pumpkin? I blamed the goats! You don't even like vegetables!
dlg.story.pumpkin.felix.1.why: sets up Felix's 'the goats were very understanding'

event.overheard_tilda_juno_2.l3.text: I know. I put the sack there your first week, years ago. Nobody's moved it since.
event.overheard_tilda_juno_2.l3.why: Juno's reply says 'Years?', so the line now gives her the years

notes: Felix's story_pumpkin_felix.after says 'with the photograph': no camera exists in the game. Suggest 'with the carp's apology' or similar (Felix's line).
Bram/Juno: the story_notes_juno fact (Bram thinks Tilda wrote Juno's six notes) fits me: I am a note writer too, so the mix-up is believable. I accept it; I will not deny or confirm in my lines.
hall_dance: Wren now says six winters and the closing narration has two separate dances; my lines carry no number. My .10 now gives Marcus the coin, which his 'One coin. One dance.' picks up.
tilda_heart10 still gives only the pie; no line promises the two-note bell. It remains a candidate for a later gift.
Lantern festival is day 25 with the bell; running fact says winter lanterns hang on the first of the month. Hanging versus releasing reads fine, but the Director may want to confirm.
